question: Why is dextrose short, and what do we do?

steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals
steps.purpose: Read on-hand stock and 28-day use where each hospital keeps it.
steps.finding: 12 stock lines across 3 hospitals, 6 presentations, in units of use.

steps.title: Where our supply is made
steps.purpose: Follow each product's label to the plants it names, and place each plant in FDA's registration file.
steps.finding: 9 plant links on 5 labels; 7 placed in FDA's registration file.

steps.title: What FDA says about this shortage
steps.purpose: Read FDA's current shortage list and its history for this drug.
steps.finding: On FDA's list as Current for 6 companies.

steps.title: Who else makes it
steps.purpose: List every labeler of this drug in the same form, and the plants their labels name.
steps.finding: 20 labelers make it in this form.

steps.title: What FDA found at those plants
steps.purpose: Read every FDA drug inspection, warning letter, import alert and recall for these plants.
steps.finding: 111 inspections (16 OAI at our plants), 7 compliance actions, 1 import-alert listings, 19 recalls.

steps.title: What FDA wrote at the OAI inspections
steps.purpose: Read the Form 483 observations recorded at those inspections.

steps.title: What our P&T committee already approved
steps.purpose: Read Corvale General's approved interchanges for these items.

steps.title: Which links can't be trusted
steps.purpose: Run the semantic layer's key rules (NDC and unit of use) over each hospital's stock, and name the rows they reject.
steps.finding: 11 stock rows across the system fail the NDC rule; 0 of them are this drug. Every row is in a shared unit of use.

steps.title: What we decided last time
steps.purpose: Recall past decisions on this drug from H-MEM, with who approved them.
steps.finding: No past decisions on this drug.

explanation.headline: FDA's records trace our supply to plants with OAI classifications and recalls before and after the 2022-01-13 shortage posting

sentences.text: FDA first posted the dextrose monohydrate shortage on 2022-01-13 and it remains current as of 2026-10-21.
Multiple manufacturers supplying our sites have FDA inspection histories that include OAI classifications and recalls both before and after the shortage posting.

B. Braun US Pharmaceutical Manufacturing LLC (FEI 2021236) received an OAI classification letter dated 2020-10-22, 448 days before the shortage posting, and a later inspection ending 2025-11-21 was also classified OAI.
Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1021343) received OAI classifications for inspections ending 2010-01-19, 2011-06-17, and 2011-08-04, with a warning letter issued 2010-04-12.

Class I recall D-1257-2020 by B. Braun Medical Inc started 2020-04-18 (635 days before posting) and Class II recall D-0076-2021 by Baxter Healthcare Corporation started 2020-10-07 (463 days before posting) both involved dextrose-containing products.

The best available option is to transfer 89 bags of 50 g/1000 mL, 250 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East, which would increase Corvale East's supply from 2.4 days to 5 days while Corvale General retains 14 days.
